subject: biology
promptStrong: Give me a 6-mark exam-style question on {lo} for {board} {level} {subject}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a worked example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Which statement correctly distinguishes prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells?
options: Eukaryotic cells have no membrane-bound nucleus
Prokaryotic cells have genetic material not enclosed in a nucleus
Prokaryotic cells are larger than eukaryotic cells
questions.explain: Prokaryotes lack a true nucleus, whereas eukaryotes (plants, animals) have membrane-bound organelles including a nucleus.

questions.q: A positive Biuret test for protein is shown by a colour change from:
questions.explain: Biuret reagent (blue) turns purple/lilac when protein is present.

questions.q: What is the correct order of the levels of organisation, smallest to largest?
questions.explain: Cells make tissues, tissues make organs, organs make organ systems.

questions.q: Why does an electron microscope allow us to see more detail than a light microscope?
options: It uses a brighter light source
It has a much higher magnification and resolution
It magnifies but has lower resolution
It only works on living cells
questions.explain: Electron microscopes have far higher magnification and resolution, revealing sub-cellular structures.

questions.q: Which feature of an alveolus does NOT help gas exchange?
questions.explain: Alveoli have thin walls (short diffusion distance), not thick ones; thin walls speed up diffusion.

questions.q: The 'lock and key' model explains that an enzyme:
options: Has an active site with a specific shape that fits a particular substrate
questions.explain: The active site has a complementary shape to its specific substrate, like a key fitting a lock.

questions.q: Lipids (fats) are broken down by lipase into:
questions.explain: Lipase breaks lipids down into fatty acids and glycerol.

questions.q: What is the role of the permanent vacuole in a plant cell?
options: Contains cell sap to keep the cell turgid (firm)
questions.explain: The vacuole is filled with cell sap and helps keep the plant cell rigid and supported.

questions.q: Root hair cells are well adapted for absorbing water because they:
options: Have a large surface area and a thin cell wall
Carry out active transport of water
questions.explain: A large surface area and thin wall maximise water uptake by osmosis (water is never moved by active transport).

questions.q: Plant roots absorb mineral ions from very dilute soil solutions by active transport because:
options: The ions move down their concentration gradient
The ions must be moved against the concentration gradient into the root
The ion concentration is higher in the soil than in the root
questions.explain: Mineral ions are usually more concentrated inside the root, so they must be moved against the gradient by active transport.

questions.q: Diffusion is best described as the movement of particles:
options: From a low to a high concentration using energy
Of water only across a membrane
From a high to a low concentration down a concentration gradient
questions.explain: Diffusion is the net movement of particles from high to low concentration, down the gradient, and is passive.

questions.q: Why is glucose absorbed from the small intestine into the blood sometimes by active transport?
options: To absorb glucose even when its concentration is higher in the blood than the gut
Glucose is always at a higher concentration in the gut
To move water into the blood
questions.explain: Active transport allows glucose to be absorbed against the gradient when blood glucose is higher than in the gut.
